header.quote: On each HTTP request that Slack sends, Slack adds an X-Slack-Signature HTTP header (or x-slack-signature

scheme.value: HMAC-SHA256 keyed with the app Signing Secret (used as a plain UTF-8 string), hex digest, prefixed with the literal v0=
scheme.quote: The full signature is formed by prefixing the hex digest with v0=, to make 'v0=a2114d57b48eac39b9ad189dd8316235a7b4a8d21a10bd27519666489c69b503'.

signed_content.value: The base string: the version v0, a colon, the value of X-Slack-Request-Timestamp, a colon, then the raw request body, i.e. v0:{timestamp}:{raw_body}
signed_content.quote: Concatenate the version number, the timestamp, and the request body together, using a colon ( : ) as a delimiter.

header_format.value: Single signature, form v0=<64 hex chars>. The page says header names are meant to be case-insensitive, so do not assume letter case.
header_format.quote: header names are meant to be case-insensitive, so the letter case should not be assumed

secret_source.value: App Signing Secret, in the app admin panel under Basic Info (Basic Information)
secret_source.quote: Grab your Slack Signing Secret, available in the app admin panel under Basic Info.
secret_source.short: Signing Secret, app settings > Basic Information

secret_scope.value: Per app (Slack creates a unique string for your app)
secret_scope.quote: Slack creates a unique string for your app and shares it with you.

timestamp_tolerance.value: Five minutes: reject if the timestamp differs from local time by more than five minutes (the page's pseudocode uses 60 * 5 seconds)
timestamp_tolerance.quote: In this example, we verify that the timestamp does not differ from local time by more than five minutes.

rotation.value: Regenerate button next to the Signing Secret in the admin panel. The page does not describe dual signatures or a grace period.
rotation.quote: Regenerate your secret using the "Regenerate" button next to the Signing Secret in the admin panel.

raw_body_note.value: Use the raw request body, before it has been deserialized from JSON or other forms.
raw_body_note.quote: Use the raw request body, without headers, before it has been deserialized from JSON or other forms

node.value: Bolt for JavaScript has built-in signing-secret verification (initialise with process.env.SLACK_SIGNING_SECRET). The page also shows createMessageAdapter(process.env.SLACK_SIGNING_SECRET) for interactions. No standalone verify function is shown.

python.value: Bolt for Python has built-in signing-secret verification. No standalone verify function is shown.
python.quote: Built-in support in Bolt for Python

dotnet.value: not stated by the provider (the page lists Bolt for JavaScript, Python and Java)
dotnet.quote: Built-in support in Bolt for Java

value.note: The page's worked example is a slash command (form-encoded body). Recomputed with HMAC-SHA256 during research: it matches.

published_test_vector.quote: In this example, the Signing Secret is 8f742231b10e8888abcd99yyyzzz85a5.

method_and_content_type.value: Events API: HTTP POST with Content-Type application/json. Interactivity (buttons, shortcuts, modals): HTTP POST, application/x-www-form-urlencoded, with a payload parameter holding JSON.
method_and_content_type.quote: we'll send an HTTP POST request to your request URL. The event will be in the Content-Type: application/json format

interactive_payload_format.value: application/x-www-form-urlencoded body with a payload field that must be parsed as JSON; every structure has a type field
interactive_payload_format.quote: They'll be sent to your specified Request URL in an HTTP POST request in the form application/x-www-form-urlencoded.

interactive_payload_parse.value: The body contains a payload parameter; parse it as JSON
interactive_payload_parse.quote: The body of the request will contain a payload parameter; your app should parse this payload parameter as JSON.

event_type_location.value: Outer envelope: top-level type (event_callback, or url_verification during setup). Event name: event.type inside the envelope.
event_type_location.quote: Typically, that is event_callback. You may encounter url_verification during the configuration process.
event_type_location.short: event.type (the top-level type is event_callback or url_verification)

event_type_inner.quote: The specific name of the event described by its adjacent fields.

delivery_id.value: event_id, a string at the top level of the envelope (for example Ev123ABC456), with event_time in epoch seconds

handshake.value: url_verification: Slack POSTs JSON {token, challenge, type: url_verification}. Respond HTTP 200 with the challenge value, either as the raw challenge string, or as application/x-www-form-urlencoded challenge=..., or as JSON {"challenge": "..."}. The request URL must be confirmed before the form can be saved.
handshake.quote: Once you receive the event, complete the sequence by responding with HTTP 200 and the challenge attribute value.
handshake.short: url_verification: answer 200 with the challenge value

batching.quote: Your request URL will receive a request for each event matching your subscriptions. One request, one event.

success_status.value: Any HTTP 2xx for Events API requests; HTTP 200 OK for interaction payloads
success_status.quote: Your app should respond to the event request with an HTTP 2xx within three seconds.

interaction_ack.value: HTTP 200 OK within 3 seconds; otherwise the Slack user sees an error
interaction_ack.quote: your app must reply to the HTTP POST request with an HTTP 200 OK response. This must be sent within 3 seconds of receiving the payload.

response_deadline.value: 3 seconds: an Events API request not answered with a 2xx within three seconds counts as a failed attempt
response_deadline.quote: Your app should respond to the event request with an HTTP 2xx within three seconds.

retries.value: Up to 3 retries: first nearly immediately, second after 1 minute, third and final after 5 minutes. Header x-slack-retry-num is 1, 2 or 3. Header x-slack-retry-reason is one of http_timeout, too_many_redirects (more than 2 redirects), ssl_error, unknown_error. Retries count against the failure limits. Optional Delayed Events setting adds hourly retries for 24 hours; by default an event more than two hours late is not delivered.
retries.quote: The first retry will be sent nearly immediately. The second retry will be attempted after 1 minute. The third and final retry will be sent after 5 minutes.
retries.short: 3 retries: almost at once, after 1 minute, after 5 minutes (opt-in hourly for 24 hours)

retry_headers.value: x-slack-retry-num (1, 2 or 3) and x-slack-retry-reason (http_timeout, too_many_redirects, ssl_error, unknown_error)
retry_headers.quote: With each retry attempt, you'll also be given a x-slack-retry-num HTTP header indicating the attempt number: 1, 2, or 3.

retry_opt_out.value: Send header x-slack-no-retry: 1 on a non-200 response to stop redelivery of that specific event

delayed_events.value: Optional Delayed Events setting: three quick retries followed by hourly retries for 24 hours; default drops events more than two hours late
delayed_events.quote: Enable the Delayed Events feature for Slack to follow those three retries with hourly retries for 24 hours.

disabling.value: Event subscriptions are temporarily disabled when failure conditions affect more than 95% of delivery attempts within 60 minutes. Apps receiving fewer than 1,000 events per hour are not auto-disabled. Re-enable via app management.
disabling.quote: When your application enters any combination of these failure conditions for more than 95% of delivery attempts within 60 minutes, your application's event subscriptions will be temporarily disabled

disabling_threshold_note.value: Keep a success response rate of at least 5% of events per 60 minutes; apps below 1,000 events per hour are exempt
disabling_threshold_note.quote: However, apps receiving less than 1,000 events per hour will not be automatically disabled.

ordering.value: not stated by the provider (the page calls the Events API best-effort and says delivery can be delayed during incidents)
ordering.quote: The Events API is a best-effort system, and event delivery could be delayed during incidents.

duplicates.value: Not stated as a guarantee either way. A retried event is sent again with x-slack-retry-num set to the attempt number.
duplicates.quote: With each retry attempt, you'll also be given a x-slack-retry-num HTTP header indicating the attempt number: 1, 2, or 3.

common.meaning: A message was posted in a channel the app can see (message.channels etc. variants exist)
common.quote: A message was sent to a channel
Subscribe to only the message events that mention your app or bot

common.meaning: A user opened the app's Home tab
common.quote: User clicked into your App Home
A user joined a public channel, private channel or MPDM

common.meaning: An emoji reaction was added to an item
common.quote: A member has added an emoji reaction to an item

common.meaning: A new member joined the workspace
Setup-time ownership challenge, not a real event
common.quote: Verifies ownership of an Events API Request URL

where_url_is_entered.value: App settings, Event Subscriptions (toggle on), then the Request URL; the URL must pass the url_verification challenge before the form saves. Interactivity has its own Request URL.
where_url_is_entered.quote: find the Event Subscriptions setting and use the toggle to turn it on.

url_confirmation.value: Request URL must be confirmed before saving; a Retry button re-attempts verification after a timeout; request URLs are case-sensitive
url_confirmation.quote: Your Event request URL must be confirmed before saving this form.

test_tools.value: not stated by the provider (the pages read mention only the Retry button for URL verification)
test_tools.quote: use the Retry button to attempt verification again.

gotchas.value: Event deliveries are capped at 30,000 per workspace per app per 60 minutes; beyond that app_rate_limited events are sent every minute.
gotchas.quote: Event deliveries currently max out at 30,000 per workspace/team per app per 60 minutes.

gotchas.value: The top-level token field is deprecated; verify with the signing secret instead.
gotchas.quote: Instead of using the token, you should rely on using signed secrets to verify requests from Slack.

gotchas.value: Compare signatures with a constant-time HMAC compare, not direct string equality.
gotchas.quote: use an hmac compare function instead of directly comparing the signatures for equality.

gotchas.value: The Events API tolerates added fields: expect extra or conditionally present fields.
gotchas.quote: to expect additional fields you haven't encountered before or fields that are only conditionally present.

gotchas.value: If one event is visible to several installed users, Slack sends it once with a single user in authorizations.
gotchas.quote: we will send one event and include one user to whom this event is "visible" in the authorizations.user_id field.
